text: Aditi is twelve weeks pregnant! Due date is around 3rd of May. She's off caffeine completely and says she misses her flat white more than wine.
Joe's band has a gig at the Lexington on 14 November. He asked if I could bring a few people. I need to sort tickets by the end of the month.
Hana is vegan now, properly, not just at home. Worth remembering before anyone books the restaurant for her birthday.
Had coffee with Angela. Her daughter Nia ran her first half marathon on Sunday and finished in just under two hours. Angela was in tears at the finish line, apparently.

Remind me to text Kofi good luck before his piano recital on 22/11. He admitted he hasn't played in front of an audience since school and is really nervous about it. It's at the community hall at 7pm, and his wife Hana has invited half the street, which is not helping. He's playing Chopin and something by Debussy. I might go if I can get out of work early.
Wei and Rafael are having the christening for baby Luca on the 7th of December. Lunch afterwards at Rafael's parents' place. I'm doing a cheesecake.
Ayo can't eat gluten, coeliac rather than a preference. Also hates coriander with a passion.
Camila mentioned her sister Marta is expecting twins in early March. Their mum is flying over from Bogotá to help for a few months.
Mei's netball team made the regional final. The match is sometime next week, she thinks Thursday. I should ask her how it went.
Luis only drinks red wine, ideally something Spanish. Good to know for Christmas.
Ioana had the baby! A girl, Elena, born on Saturday morning, 3.2kg. Ioana says she is exhausted but happy. Don't forget to send a card and something small for the baby.
Lachlan is running the Edinburgh marathon at the end of May. He's raising money for the hospice that looked after his dad. Must sponsor him.

Emeka's wife Julia is struggling a bit since the baby arrived. Not sleeping, feeling low. He asked if I knew anyone who'd been through it. I should check in on her sometime next week, maybe drop round with food. Julia likes that Thai place on the high street, and she's off dairy while breastfeeding, so I'll need to check the menu. Emeka goes back to work on 17 November, which is probably when she'll need people most.
Jonah is lactose intolerant but will happily eat cheese and suffer. His words.
Lars told me his play opens on 12 March at the Corn Exchange and runs until the 16th. He's playing the lead. I'd like to go on the Friday.

Laila's baby shower was meant to be this Saturday but it's been called off because she's on bed rest. Her mum Svetlana says the doctors want her to take it easy until the due date, which is early January. Laila is bored out of her mind and fed up of daytime TV. Svetlana suggested we do a small video call party instead sometime next week. I could send her a box of books and those ginger biscuits she likes.
Reggie is a huge Arsenal fan, season ticket and everything. He's going to the derby on 23/11 with his son.
Called Joseph about the quiz. He's off alcohol for Sober October, so soft drinks only for him at the pub on Thursday.

Karim is doing a triathlon over the summer, his first one. He's terrified of the open water swim. He said he would love a wetsuit for his birthday, though I think he was half joking. His girlfriend Ioana is doing the cycling leg with him as a relay team, and they've been training together at the lido every Sunday. The race is in Windermere, probably mid-July, but they haven't booked it yet.
Abdi and his wife are expecting their second baby in the spring. Their eldest, Yusuf, is four and apparently not thrilled about it.
Hassan's daughter has her violin grade 5 exam on 2nd of December. He says she practises every night and drives the neighbours mad.
Graham is diabetic, type 2, diagnosed last year. Bear that in mind with puddings when he comes for dinner.
Kieran Chen came second in the chess tournament in Leeds at the weekend. Need to congratulate him properly when I see him on Friday.
Ebony is pregnant again! Due in late April. She told me before she's told her boss, so keep quiet. She's craving pickled onions, of all things.
Kemal's mum makes the best baklava. He brought some to work today. Must ask for the recipe.
Nia has a dance competition in Blackpool on 30 November. Her dad is driving the whole team down. She has been rehearsing every weekend since September.

Aditi's husband Kofi is cooking a big Sunday lunch on the 9th of November to celebrate the scan going well. They both want to keep it small, just close friends. I'm bringing dessert, but nothing with nuts because Aditi is allergic.
Bought the tickets for the jazz night at Ronnie's. Need to pick up a birthday card for Mum on the way home.
Joe Smith, or Smithy as everyone at football calls him, has finally agreed to join the Sunday league team. First match is 2 November.

Hana's partner Lachlan was telling me she is training for a 10k sometime in the spring. She doesn't know he told me. She has been eyeing up new running shoes, so that could be a nice birthday present.
Angela can't stand spicy food. Mild everything. Keep that in mind when choosing the curry house for the leaving do.

Lunch with Wei. His wife Mei is due on 18 December, and he's started paternity leave planning at work. He seems calm, but she's worried about the birth after a difficult first pregnancy. I should message her this weekend to see how she's doing.
Grocery run tomorrow: oat milk, eggs, the decaf beans from the market. Also renew the car insurance before the 28th.
Rafael's choir concert was brilliant last night. Everyone stood up at the end. I should send him the video I took.
Ayo told me she's been made captain of the hockey team. The first league game under her captaincy is on 8th of November.
Camila doesn't drink at all, never has. She likes elderflower cordial, though, and those fancy sodas.
Luis and Ioana are hosting a gender reveal party sometime at the end of the month. Date to be confirmed. Ioana wants everyone to wear either pink or blue, which feels like a lot.

Spoke to Svetlana after book club. Her grandson Kemal is getting christened on 15/12 in Bucharest. She's flying out a week early to help with the food. Remind me to ask her for the address so I can post a gift.

Marta has pre-eclampsia, they found out at the scan yesterday. She's being monitored twice a week now. Her husband Karim sounded shaken on the phone. Need to call her tomorrow evening. Karim said the doctors might deliver early if her blood pressure keeps climbing, possibly as soon as the end of the month. Their mum is staying with them, which helps. I should also ask Karim whether they need anyone to walk the dog.
Laila's brother Hassan is taking part in a cooking competition on local TV in early February. He specialises in Lebanese food. I said I'd watch.
Julia loves a negroni. Gin, Campari, the lot. Bitter is her thing, she says, sweet cocktails are wasted on her.
Emeka mentioned his niece is starting at a stage school in London in January. She got in after three auditions. The whole family is very proud.
Lars's boxing match got cancelled at the last minute because his opponent pulled out injured. He's gutted, but he'll be rebooked sometime next month.

Reggie and his wife Angela are celebrating their twentieth wedding anniversary on 5th of June with a big party in the garden. They've invited about sixty people. Angela said there will be a ceilidh band and a hog roast, and they've asked people to bring a dish for the dessert table. I should start thinking about what to make, and also chip in for the group present. Graham is collecting money until the middle of May.
Joseph's partner Abdi is a pescatarian, but eats chicken occasionally if it's a special meal. Make sure there's a fish option on the 21st.
Graham's granddaughter was born on Tuesday. He showed me about forty photos. Her name is Ruby.
Kieran's cat Biscuit had an operation on his leg this morning. Kieran was really anxious about it. Biscuit is home now and sleeping it off. Must text Kieran tomorrow to see how the little guy is.
Ebony's son is in the school nativity play on 12 December. He's playing a sheep and is, according to Ebony, taking it very seriously.
I'm going to the Brighton half marathon on 22 February to support Nia. Booked the train already.
Kemal Yilmaz is gluten free and dairy free, and doesn't eat pork. I need to tell the caterers before the 3rd of November.
Aditi asked if I'd be godmother to the baby. I said yes, obviously. The christening is pencilled in for early June, after the baby is born at the start of May.
Mei is doing the Great North Run in September with her brother Jonah. They're both raising money for a children's charity. He's done it three times; it's her first, and she's worried about her knee.

Long chat with Hana on the phone tonight. She's 30 weeks now and the nursery is finally painted. She's been craving watermelon and can't stand the smell of coffee anymore. Her mum is coming to stay from the 1st of December until after the birth, which Hana is quite relieved about, honestly. The baby shower is on 16/11 at her friend Camila's flat. Need to buy something from the registry before the end of next week, and I should ask Camila if she needs help with decorations.
Kofi's cycling race in the Peak District went well on Saturday. He came eighth out of about two hundred. He's already talking about next year.
Wei's dog Mochi had puppies last week, five of them. He's keeping one and finding homes for the rest. I'm tempted.
Rafael is cutting out sugar for a month because his doctor told him his blood sugar is borderline. Don't bring cake to his on Saturday.
Clear out the garage this weekend and drop the old cot at the charity shop.

Luis said his little brother is competing at the national swimming championships in Sheffield from 8 to 10 April. He's only fifteen. He's been training at 5am every day for two years, so the whole family is going up to watch. Luis is taking the Friday off work. I should text Luis on the Saturday to see how the heats went.
Ioana's mother-in-law has offered to look after Elena two days a week from February when Ioana goes back to work. Ioana isn't sure how she feels about it.

Saw Lachlan, Ayo and Laila at Emeka's barbecue. Lachlan is lactose intolerant, Ayo is doing Veganuary again in January, and Laila's waters broke last night! Baby boy, Adam, born at 4am today. Must send her flowers and a card sometime next week once she's home and settled.
